Maya: Heads-up — saw an 8-12% regression on the GQA path after the KV-cache layout change (paged -> contiguous). Profiling shows the kernel selector picking the generic MHA kernel for long sequences. cc @Ryan @Li

Ryan: Can you drop the bench numbers + env? which model and seq lengths?

Maya: Microbench details:
```
model: gpt-j-like (~6B)
hardware: p3.2xlarge-ish (A100)
batch: 1
before (paged layout): seq=512 -> 920 tokens/s
after (contiguous layout): seq=512 -> 840 tokens/s  // -8.7%
seq=64 -> 2900 -> 2880 tokens/s  // ~-0.7% (no issue)
MQA path: seq=512 -> 1500 -> 1450 tokens/s // ~-3.3%
```
Looks correlated with seq_len >= 256.

Li: Hmm — that smells like the selector thresholds we tuned assume a paged KV layout and its associated block-friendly kernels. PR #432 changed the KV page remap; we didn't surface kv_layout/block_size into the kernel selection key. Right now the chooser is basically:
```
key = (arch, model_dim, head_dim, seq_len_bucket)
pick = autotune_table[key] or fallback_generic
```
We should include kv_layout and kv_block_size into the key so autotune can pick paged-optimized kernels.

Sam: Profiler showed a jump in L2 miss rate and some extra memcpy hotspots when contiguous layout is used with block-optimized kernels. Suggest we run an autotune matrix across: arch x seq_bins x kv_block_size x batch_bucket.

perf-bot: Scheduled microbench ran at 10:12Z. Short summary: gqa_mha_kernel_v2 regresses for seq >= 256 when kv_layout=contiguous. Detailed logs uploaded to /tmp/perf/gqa_kv_layout_176999.log

Infra-bot: If we change selector logic we'll want a canary. Recommend flagging rollout as `kernel_autotune:kv-layout-v1` and apply to a single dedicated pool first.

Maya: Proposed action plan:
1) Add kv_layout and kv_block_size to kernel selection key
2) Extend autotune sweep: seq_bins=[32,64,128,256,512], kv_block=[32,64,128], batch_buckets=[1,2-8,>8]
3) Run microbench across representative models (gpt-j-like, llama-13B-ish, and one MQA-trained model)
4) If new table increases tail latency > +15% on any canary, revert selector for that pool
Start experiments now, will post results.

Ryan: I can implement the selector change. Proposed pseudo patch:
```
struct KernelKey { arch, model_dim, head_dim, seq_bin, kv_layout, kv_block, batch_bucket };
auto choose_kernel(key) {
  if (autotune_table.contains(key)) return autotune_table[key];
  // heuristic fallback prefers paged-optimized kernels when kv_layout==PAGED
  if (key.kv_layout==PAGED && key.seq_bin >= 128) return paged_opt_kernel;
  return generic_mha;
}
```
I'll open a PR and tag @Li for microbench harness changes.

Li: I'll add L2/L3 counters and memcpy traces to the bench script. Expecting runs in ~2 hours, will attach CSV + flamegraphs. Also will include per-kernel selection logs so we can see which kernel was chosen at runtime.

Sam: Also flagging that batching heuristics interact with this — smaller batches increase per-token kernel overhead and can flip the preferred kernel. We should include batch_bucket in the key (as Maya suggested).

Maya: Agreed — include {1, 2-8, >8} buckets. Also add a quick guard: if chosen kernel increases median latency by >10% in the microbench, fallback to previous kernel automatically.

Ryan: Pushed branch `kernel-select/kv-meta`. PR in draft, linking bench infra in description.

Maya: Thanks. I'll watch perf-bot and the canary. If we get stable wins for paged-optimized kernels with kv_block=64 for seq >=256 we can make that the default for those models. :eyes:

perf-bot: Noted — will post aggregated numbers every 30m.

Infra-bot: Once PR lands, we can add a canary target in `dedicated-pool-2` and a feature-flag rollout.

Maya: Great. Quick TODOs: Ryan - PR, Li - bench + counters, Sam - validate batch interaction, I'll coordinate canary and rollback policy.

Ryan: On it.

Li: Starting runs now.

Sam: Lgtm. :thumbsup:
